fatal_errors: The cited evidence only evaluates a different CuMoTaWV film at room temperature and 300 °C; it does not support stable lubrication, coating adhesion, or wear protection at 800 °C.
Formation of a lubricious CuO-based film across the full temperature range is asserted without supporting phase, friction, or oxidation evidence.
The proposed 1 N testing condition does not reproduce the relevant 8 N sliding regime, so success would not establish performance under the target mechanical boundary.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad engineering objective and gives a testable coating-based alternative, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention of varying Mo in CoCrFeNiMox–Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 SPS composites. It therefore misses the target structural mediators—Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature silver-molybdate glaze formation—as well as the specified 8 N, 0.15 m/s, 270 m, Si3N4-counterbody conditions. The baseline is qualitative and provides no starting friction or wear values. Its predicted 30–50% improvement at every temperature is insufficiently justified, particularly because the cited work stops at 300 °C and concerns different substrates and counterbodies. The proposed coated-versus-uncoated comparison is falsifiable and includes useful tribological and surface measurements, but it should include coating-only, annealing-only, and Cu-free controls and denser temperature sampling. Overall, this is a scientifically conceivable alternative rather than an evidence-supported reconstruction of the hidden paper.
